questions.prompt: What is the core mistake in base-rate neglect?
choices: Giving one vivid case more weight than the broader frequency pattern
Ignoring every individual detail in favor of statistics
Assuming all cases are identical

explanation.gentle: Yes. The specific case is being allowed to crowd out the wider pattern.
explanation.direct: Correct. The vivid example is receiving more influence than the base rate that should frame it.
explanation.competitive: That is the trap. One story is passing for the whole field.

questions.prompt: Why can this bias feel persuasive?
choices: Because one detailed story feels more concrete than an abstract population pattern
Because general frequencies are always less relevant than individual cases
Because vivid examples automatically represent the majority

explanation.gentle: Right. The case feels more alive than the background pattern.
explanation.direct: Exactly. Specific detail is easier to picture and trust than an abstract rate or distribution.
explanation.competitive: That is it. The anecdote has a face while the base rate looks like paperwork.

questions.prompt: Which situation best fits base-rate neglect?
choices: A person lets one striking example outweigh what usually happens across the broader population
A team combines a case with background data before deciding
A student reviews several representative examples together

explanation.gentle: Yes. One case is replacing the wider pattern.
explanation.direct: Correct. The judgment is being driven by case vividness more than by base-rate context.
explanation.competitive: That is the move. The story is benching the population.

questions.prompt: A hiring team becomes convinced by one unusual candidate story. What should they check first?
choices: Whether the story feels vivid enough to justify a special conclusion
Whether the story fits the broader hiring pattern or merely feels memorable
Whether rare candidates automatically outperform common ones

explanation.gentle: Yes. They need the wider pattern back before trusting the case too much.
explanation.direct: That is the key. The team should compare the vivid candidate story with the broader pool of relevant outcomes.
explanation.competitive: Exactly. Make the story fight with the whole hiring field before it gets the offer.

questions.prompt: A teacher treats one poor performance as if it defines the student. What is most likely happening?
choices: The single case is crowding out the broader distribution of the student's work
One result always reveals the deepest truth
Base rates no longer matter once a result is emotional

explanation.gentle: Right. One performance is replacing the wider pattern.
explanation.direct: The likely distortion is that a vivid result is being weighted more than the student's broader base rate of performance.
explanation.competitive: That is the bias. One clip is trying to rewrite the whole reel.

questions.prompt: What is the cleanest practical correction when one story feels unusually persuasive?
choices: Assume the story is representative because it is memorable
Restore the base rate before letting the story dominate the conclusion
Ignore all case details completely

explanation.gentle: Yes. The broader pattern needs to come back into view.
explanation.direct: That correction works because it forces the vivid case to be judged against what normally happens.
explanation.competitive: Exactly. Drag the population back in before the story locks the verdict.

questions.prompt: Which statement stays inside this chapter's boundary?
choices: Case details never matter once statistics appear
Specific examples matter, but they should not erase the broader population pattern
One unusual case usually reveals more than the base rate

explanation.gentle: Right. The chapter is about restoring context, not erasing the case.
explanation.direct: That keeps the boundary intact: individual detail matters, but it should be interpreted inside the broader frequency pattern.
explanation.competitive: Exactly. The story can stay, but it does not get to own the whole field.

questions.prompt: Why can a vivid case overpower the base rate?
choices: Because representativeness and vividness can feel stronger than abstract background frequency
Because the wider population is never useful once a case is known
Because abstract information is automatically false

explanation.gentle: Yes. The vivid case feels more real even when the broader pattern still matters.
explanation.direct: The danger is that narrative force makes the case easier to trust than the colder but still essential background distribution.
explanation.competitive: That is the issue. The high-definition example can outshout the wider field.

questions.prompt: A manager wants to test whether the team is overreacting to one anecdote. Which earlier chapter pairs best with base-rate neglect here?
choices: Neglect of Probability, because both chapters warn against letting what feels vivid outrun broader quantitative reality
Scarcity Error, because scarcity always causes anecdotes
Groupthink, because base rates only disappear in groups

explanation.gentle: Yes. Both chapters warn against letting vividness overpower the larger numerical frame that should guide judgment.
explanation.direct: This pairing works because each bias lets emotionally available information dominate the broader quantitative context.
explanation.competitive: That is the strongest link. A hot story or hot scenario can both fake more weight than the wider numbers justify.

questions.prompt: A sound judgment about a vivid case survives which test?
choices: The case still feels memorable after retelling it
The conclusion still holds after the broader base rate is restored beside the case
The case is unusual enough to ignore the wider population

explanation.gentle: Yes. The wider pattern should still support the conclusion once it returns to view.
explanation.direct: That is the decisive test because it shows whether the case remains persuasive after population-level context is restored.
explanation.competitive: Exactly. If the verdict folds when the base rate walks back in, the story was doing fake work.
